feature: Resizing a stack shows the box you are making
summary: Drag a handle on a group that arranges itself and the box you are making is now drawn on the canvas for as long as the button is down, as the same grey hairline a screen wears at its edge. Before this, a stack's rows did not move and the group had no edge, so a whole drag changed nothing on screen and the only sign anything was happening was the width in the right hand panel.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Groups that arrange their own contents must be on in Experiments; it is on by default.

try.do: Draw three rectangles one under the other, all about the same width.
Select all three and press Control Command G to stack them.
Press the bottom right handle of the stack and drag it out, slowly, without letting go.
Watch the canvas rather than the panel: a thin grey box should be following your hand.
Let go, and check the rows and the box landed where the hairline was.
Now drag the same handle back in, past the left edge of the rows, and let go.
Do the same drag on a plain group and on a frame, and see that neither picked up a second edge.

evaluate: While you are dragging, can you tell what size you are choosing without looking at the right hand panel?
Does the hairline land exactly where the stack lands, or does the box jump on release?
Is a grey hairline the right weight here, or does the box want to be more obviously temporary, for example dashed?
Pulled in narrower than its rows, the box goes smaller than what is inside it and the rows hang out: is that the right thing to show, or should it refuse?
Does a plain group still feel fine without one, since its contents scale under your hand anyway?
rough: The Mac's screen was locked for this whole task, so no walk could run and no picture of the window was possible: there is no screenshot here, and none of this was seen on a real canvas. The rule behind the box has thirteen tests of its own and the whole suite is green, but nobody has watched the hairline follow a hand yet. A sweep has been asked for so the walk runs the moment the screen is unlocked.
The box is axis aligned, so a stack that has been turned would get a straight box round a slanted group. Frame edges have the same limit today, so this is not new, but it is not right either.

A copy of a component that is itself a left aligned stack still shows nothing: its pieces are placed rather than flowed, so most copies do move under the hand, but a hugging one would not. It was left out because the task asked for copies to behave exactly as they do today.

The hairline is the same grey as a screen's edge on purpose, so the canvas has one voice for a container's edge. The other reading is that a box which only exists while your hand is down should look temporary, and that is a real choice somebody should make by looking at it.
